headline: FRIEDLAND'S IVANHOE ELECTRIC DRILLS 123.6m AT 0.91% Cu NEAR BISBEE — New Arizona Copper-Gold-Silver Breccia Zone Among Best Results in Western US in a Decade
snippet: Ivanhoe Electric (TSX: IE) reported a 123.6-metre intercept at 0.91% copper, 0.44 g/t gold and 5.27 g/t silver from 601.70m in hole CGD26-TR-003 at its Gleeson project in southeastern Arizona — with a high-grade sub-interval of 71.03 metres averaging 1.38% Cu — alongside a second hole returning 381.66 metres at 0.34% Cu from 587.85m. The company described these as among the best copper-gold-silver results drilled anywhere in the western United States in the past decade. Gleeson sits 28 miles north of the historic Bisbee district, with the discovery breccia zone now defined over approximately 500 by 500 metres and open in multiple directions; two rigs are active with a 16,000-metre drill target by year-end 2026.

headline: COLLECTIVE MINING DRILLS 146m AT 1.07 g/t AuEq AT APOLLO SHALLOW HALO ZONE — Extension Pushes 60 Metres Beyond Resource Boundary; 92% Hit Rate on 64 SHZ Holes
snippet: Collective Mining (TSX: CNL) released assays from 17 diamond holes extending the Apollo deposit's Shallow Halo Zone in Colombia, with the lead intercept returning 146.10 metres at 1.07 g/t gold-equivalent from 106.50m — including 6.75 metres at 11.15 g/t AuEq — pushing the zone 60 metres beyond the September 8 mineral resource boundary. With 59 of 64 total SHZ holes (92%) returning above-grade intervals since the resource announcement, the company is building a systematic case for a material resource expansion. For junior mining investors, this hit rate on a resource expansion program is exceptionally high, and the shallow depth of mineralization adds optionality for near-surface open-pit development scenarios.

headline: PHOENIX METALS HITS 169m AT 1.30% CuEq IN FIRST-EVER LEXINGTON HOLE — BC Copper-Gold Target Delivers Grade From Just 41m Depth
snippet: Phoenix Metals (TSX: PCA) reported its first drill results from the Lexington Target in British Columbia: hole LXDDH-26-001 returned 169 metres at 1.30% copper-equivalent (0.22% Cu, 1.02 g/t Au, 3.79 g/t Ag) starting from just 41 metres depth — a genuinely impressive first hole for a new target, where shallow high-grade mineralization dramatically improves project economics. The result opens a new BC copper-gold system that the company will now prioritize for step-out drilling to define the lateral and depth extent. For retail mining investors, a first drill hole that hits grade over 169 metres near-surface is rare enough that it typically re-rates the company when the broader market is paying attention.

headline: CANTEX CUTS 27.39% Pb-Zn AND 2.4 g/t GOLD AT NORTH RACKLA YUKON — Every Drill Hole Hits Mineralization in New North Gold Target Phase
snippet: Cantex Mine Development (TSX-V: CD) reported that all three diamond holes drilled at the North Gold Target within its North Rackla project in Yukon successfully intersected mineralization, returning up to 2.4 g/t gold and up to 27.39% combined lead-zinc. The North Rackla area has historically been among Canada's most prospective underexplored polymetallic belts, and a 100% hit rate in a first-pass drill program at a new target signals genuine geological coherence rather than isolated high-grade lenses. Investors tracking Yukon critical mineral and precious metal exploration should note that the project's existing infrastructure and established drill contractor relationships allow rapid capital allocation when results justify follow-up.

headline: AMERICAN CRITICAL MINERALS HITS 38.51% KCl IN UTAH'S FIRST HOLE — Paradox Basin Potash Grades 51% Higher Than Nearby Historical Well at Green River
snippet: American Critical Minerals (CSE: KCLI / OTCQB: APCOF) announced its first drill hole at the Green River Project in Utah's Paradox Basin returned 6.55 metres grading 38.51 wt.% KCl — with a high-grade composite of 42.94 wt.% over 2.1 metres — representing an 11% increase in thickness and a 51% increase in grade versus the historic Quintana Fed 1-1 well located approximately 600 metres away. The result establishes the geological model and confirms the Cycle 5 potash member as a viable drill target. Potash is a critical agricultural fertilizer input largely controlled by Russian and Belarusian producers, making new domestic North American deposits a strategic supply chain priority; lithium and bromine brine zones were also reached but remain under evaluation.

headline: NORTH ARROW TRACES 48m OF 0.63 g/t GOLD AT TLOU — Deepest Botswana Hole Ends in Mineralization; Kraaipan Resource Footprint Continues to Grow
snippet: North Arrow Minerals (TSX-V: NAR) reported that drill hole KR26-108 returned 48 metres grading 0.63 g/t gold at the Tlou target within its Kraaipan Gold Project in Botswana, with the deepest hole drilled to date ending in open mineralization — signaling that the system extends beyond the current drill depth. Broad, shallow mineralization in the Kraaipan greenstone belt is building a framework consistent with bulk-mineable open-pit style gold at scale; the project covers approximately 724 square kilometres of the northern extension of the Kraaipan belt, most of which remains undrilled. For junior mining investors, Botswana remains one of Africa's most mining-friendly jurisdictions, with stable permitting and direct rail access to South African ports.

headline: VAL-D'OR MINING ASSAYS 59.52 g/t GOLD IN PERESTROIKA DRILL — High-Grade VMS Vein Extends at Quebec JV With Eldorado Gold
snippet: Val-D'Or Mining (TSX-V: VZZ) reported a 1.15-metre interval averaging 59.52 g/t gold at the Perestroika Prospect within the Val-D'Or mining camp in Quebec, part of a joint venture in which VZZ holds 70% and Eldorado Gold (TSX: ELD) holds 30%. The result extends a high-grade VMS-style vein system within one of Canada's most historically productive gold camps. While the intersection width is narrow, 59.52 g/t gold over 1.15m delivers significant metal content per tonne of ore — a characteristic typical of VMS vein systems that must be evaluated against the broader corridor geometry rather than individual intercept widths alone.

headline: LEGACY GOLD EXTENDS BANER MAIN ZONE TO 3,543 FEET — Idaho Gold System Grows Near Surface With 41m At 0.35 g/t Au; NW Zone Opens New Corridor
snippet: Legacy Gold Mines (TSX-V: LEGY) extended the Main Zone at its Baner gold project in Idaho to 3,543 feet (1,080 metres) with a near-surface intercept of 41.1 metres at 0.35 g/t gold, while simultaneously opening a new NW Zone corridor with its first hole returning 8.9 metres at 0.37 g/t gold. The project is located in Idaho's Basin and Range province, an underexplored region for open-pittable gold compared to Nevada; continued Main Zone extensions of this scale begin to define a system geometry that could support a National Instrument 43-101 resource estimate in coming seasons. US-domiciled gold projects have attracted incremental investor interest as supply chain security concerns elevate domestic asset premiums.

headline: RSI FOR MINING STOCKS DROPS BELOW 30 — AND IT'S NOT A BUY SIGNAL YET; December Fed Hike Risk Keeps Sector Under Pressure
snippet: An Investing.com technical analysis confirms that the RSI for the gold mining sector has dropped below 30 — the threshold conventionally defined as oversold — but argues that this reading alone does not constitute a reliable buy signal ahead of the December 9 FOMC decision. The analysis notes that RSI can remain below 30 for extended periods when a macro rate catalyst is unresolved, and that the gold mining sector's RSI has stayed sub-30 for 60-day+ periods during prior tightening cycles. The piece identifies three confirmation signals investors should wait for before treating the technical extreme as a floor: a Fed pivot or pause signal, a dollar index rollover, and positive price action in GDX on above-average volume — none of which are currently present.

headline: GOLD'S LOSING STREAK PUTS 10 MINING STOCKS ON OVERSOLD WATCH — Barrick, GoldMining, Orla Among Names With RSI Below 30 as GDX Tests Multi-Month Lows
snippet: Seeking Alpha identified 10 gold mining stocks that have entered RSI-below-30 oversold territory during the current losing streak in spot gold, including Barrick Mining, GoldMining Inc., and Orla Mining, alongside the GDX and GDXJ ETFs at multi-month lows. The RSI readings across the group range from 28 to 34 — technically oversold but not yet at the extreme 15–20 levels that have historically preceded sharp recoveries. The analysis frames the watchlist as a monitoring tool rather than a buy signal: historically, the most reliable entry points in gold mining selloffs have come after RSI bottoms and reverses rather than on the initial dip below 30, suggesting patience is warranted for retail investors building mining positions through the December FOMC window.
